title: Workout application: logging, timers, substitutions, offline-first persistence
steps:
OFFLINE-FIRST WORKOUT STATE & SYNC (PRD §9, §15, §18; docs/milestones.md M4). Read the M3 logged-training schema (completed workouts, set records with unique client mutation ids, running/other sessions) and src/lib/client (M1 scaffold) first.
- Client store in src/lib/client using IndexedDB via the `idb` package (small): the active workout (planned session snapshot, current exercise index, completed/edited/skipped sets, extra sets, missed reps, substitutions, notes), rest-timer and stopwatch state (persist absolute timestamps, never tick counters, so a closed tab resumes correctly), and an OUTBOX of mutations each with a client-generated idempotency id (crypto.randomUUID) and created_at.
- Every user action writes IndexedDB first (synchronously reflected in UI state — optimistic), then the outbox flushes to the server in order with retry + exponential backoff + jitter; flush triggers: action, `online`, visibilitychange to visible, app start. Server endpoints/form actions apply mutations idempotently (ON CONFLICT on the client mutation id) and return the canonical rows; edits/deletes of a set are mutations too. Never create duplicates (same mutation sent twice, two tabs, retry after timeout where the server already committed).
- Restore: on app start or refresh mid-workout, the active workout and timers restore exactly from IndexedDB without waiting for the network; if the server has newer data (another device), reconcile deterministically (document the rule: server canonical rows + pending local mutations replayed).
- Failed sync recovery: a mutation rejected permanently (validation) is surfaced to the owner with a fix/discard action; transient failures keep retrying; a visible but unobtrusive sync status indicator (synced / saving / offline — N pending).
- Sign-out (M2) must clear this IndexedDB data — keep that test green.
- Core workout logging NEVER depends on the AI agent or any LLM call.
- Tests: unit tests for the outbox/reconciliation logic (fake IndexedDB e.g. `fake-indexeddb` in Vitest); integration tests for idempotent endpoints against Postgres (duplicate mutation ids → single row; out-of-order delivery; edit after create).

WORKOUT SCREEN & LOGGING UX (PRD §7, §8, §16 workout-specific; this is the most important screen of the product — it must feel instantaneous and be usable one-handed between heavy sets).
- Start a planned session from Today/Train (or an ad-hoc session). Strength view per exercise: name, target sets × reps, target RPE, prescribed weight (or RPE-based instruction in baseline weeks), previous performance for this exercise (last session's sets) inline for comparison, per-set rows. Logging a set: prefilled weight/reps from the prescription or last set, big NumberSteppers and quick-select RPE chips (6–10 with halves), one tap to complete; edit a completed set, skip a set, record missed reps, add extra sets; swipe/next to move between exercises; how fast the next exercise is understood is a design goal.
- Rest timer starts automatically on set completion with the prescribed rest (configurable defaults per exercise type and in settings); visible while browsing the exercise; start/pause/reset/skip/+30s; survives refresh/close (timestamp-based); optional haptic/vibration + sound where supported and allowed; a workout stopwatch for total duration.
- Plate calculator (M1 component) reachable from each set row, pre-filled with the set weight; configurable bar and available plates persisted per device; visual plate representation; lb and kg.
- Substitutions with quick actions per exercise: machine unavailable (situational — recorded on this session only), I don't like this exercise (persistent dislike via the M3 preference service, with confirmation), this hurts (never 'push through': offer a safer alternative from the substitution group or stopping the movement, record a pain note; no medical diagnosis), suggest an alternative, skip exercise. Alternatives preserve the movement pattern / muscles / training intent and respect equipment, injuries and dislikes.
- Running session logging: distance, duration, auto-computed pace, HR optional, RPE, notes; structured multi-segment runs (warmup, intervals with repeats, recovery, cooldown) with per-segment actuals. General/Muay Thai sessions: type, duration, RPE, notes, custom metrics (rounds, sparring yes/no…).
- Complete workout: summary (volume, PRs/e1RM estimates from logged sets with RPE — clearly marked estimated, duration, session RPE), notes; then History: list of completed workouts and a workout detail view; exercise history view (last performances).
- States: interrupted workout banner on Today ('Resume workout'), empty history, offline indicator, sync errors. Accessibility: axe zero violations both themes; 44px+ targets; works with large text.
- Performance: logging a set must update the UI in < 100 ms (optimistic) — measure it in Playwright with performance marks (record median and p95 over 20 sets at 4× CPU) and record real numbers in docs/performance.md; INP on the workout screen ≤ 200 ms locally (web-vitals INP in a Playwright run with real interactions at 4× CPU); route JS ≤ 60 KB gzip (lazy-load the plate calculator, history charts etc.); no layout shift while logging.

END-TO-END PROOF & PERSISTENCE VERIFICATION (PRD §18, §19). Playwright (authenticated fixture; Chromium + WebKit where the APIs allow; iPhone viewport) journeys with screenshots of every workout state saved for review:
1. Start the planned week-1 baseline workout → log sets with weight/reps/RPE → rest timer runs and survives a refresh → plate calculator from a set → substitute an exercise as 'machine unavailable' (no persistent preference created) → refresh mid-workout and verify exact restoration (current exercise, completed sets, timers) → complete the workout → see it in History and in the exercise history.
2. Offline: go offline mid-workout (context.setOffline), log several sets, reload while offline (service worker serves the shell + workout route), sets still there; go online → outbox syncs → server has exactly one row per set (query Postgres) → no duplicates even when a mutation is replayed.
3. Failed sync recovery: make the server reject a mutation (test route or route interception returning 500 then 200) → retries succeed without duplicates; a permanently invalid mutation is surfaced and can be discarded.
4. Running session with segments and a Muay Thai session logged and visible in history.
5. 'I don't like this exercise' persists and the exercise is not prescribed again in the next generated/edited week; 'this hurts' offers safer alternatives and never 'push through' copy (assert text).
Also: the service worker must cache the workout route's code so an active workout works offline (pages with personal data still not stored as HTML — data comes from IndexedDB). Update docs (architecture: offline sync design + ADR, performance with measured numbers, testing, milestones).
acceptance: Playwright: start workout, log sets/reps/RPE, rest timer, plate calculator from a set, substitute an unavailable exercise, refresh mid-workout and restore exactly (exercise, sets, timers), complete workout, view workout and exercise history — on an iPhone viewport.

Offline-first persistence: IndexedDB store + outbox with idempotent client mutation ids; offline logging survives reload; reconnect syncs; failed-sync recovery (transient retry, permanent errors surfaced); Postgres shows no duplicate sets even when mutations are replayed — proven by e2e and integration tests.
Logging a set is optimistic with measured < 100 ms to visual confirmation (median and p95 over 20 sets at 4× CPU recorded in docs/performance.md) and never depends on the AI agent or network.
INP ≤ 200 ms on the workout screen in local measurements with real interactions (number recorded), route JS ≤ 60 KB gzip, budgets and perf guard green.

Substitutions: 'machine unavailable' is situational only; 'I don't like this' persists and is not re-prescribed; 'this hurts' never suggests pushing through and offers safer alternatives or stopping; alternatives preserve movement pattern/intent and respect equipment/injuries/dislikes — tested.
Running sessions with structured segments and general/Muay Thai sessions with custom metrics can be logged, synced and viewed in history.

Rest timer and stopwatch are timestamp-based, survive refresh/close, support start/pause/reset/skip/+30s and configurable defaults; plate calculator supports bar/plate configuration in lb and kg with a visual plate stack.

The workout screen and related states (active, rest, between exercises, offline, sync error, completed summary, history, interrupted-workout resume) are premium, fast to read mid-set and usable one-handed; axe zero violations in dark and light; screenshots reviewed.
Sign-out still clears all workout data on the device; core logging works with the AI disabled.

All gates pass locally (check, lint, unit, integration, both builds, budgets, full e2e incl. perf project); docs updated (offline sync ADR, performance measurements, testing, milestones); work committed on feat/m4-workout-app with Conventional Commits.
